official_source.title: Nazarbayev University Entrance Test MATHEMATICS SPECIFICATION

subcategory.description: Divide a given quantity into two (or more) parts in a given part:part ratio. Express the division of a quantity into two parts as a ratio.

assessment.dominant_operation: Divide the known teddy-bear total among three shares with equal weighted multiples.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The unknowns are parts of one fixed total, rather than a general direct/inverse proportional law.

subcategory.description: Use fractions, decimals and percentages interchangeably in calculations. Understand equivalent fractions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Undo successive fractional parts and calculate a percentage of the same number.
assessment.why_not_alternative: There is no contextual percentage increase or decrease.

subcategory.description: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors (divisors), multiples, common factors, common multiples, highest common factor, lowest common multiple, and prime factorisation (including use of product notation and the unique factorisation theorem).

assessment.dominant_operation: Use the divisor relationship between 119 and 17 to transfer a remainder.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The decisive fact is divisibility by a factor, not merely carrying out a division.

subcategory.description: Rearrange formulae to change the subject.

assessment.dominant_operation: Isolate c in a formula containing fractional powers.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Index laws support changing the subject, which is the explicit objective.

subcategory.description: Simplify expressions involving sums, products and powers, including the laws of indices. Simplify rational expressions by cancelling, or factorising and cancelling. Use the four rules on algebraic rational expressions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Factor and cancel a symbolic quotient of functions involving a square root.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The expression has a variable and rational algebraic structure, not a purely numerical surd.

subcategory.description: Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π. Simplify surd expressions involving squares, e.g. √12 = √(4×3) = √4√3 = 2√3, and rationalise denominators; for example, candidates could be asked to rationalise expressions such as: 3/√7, 5/(3+2√5), 7/(2−√3), 3/(√5−√2).

assessment.dominant_operation: Decompose a numerical nested surd and combine its component reciprocals.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Algebraic equalities support exact surd manipulation rather than a general equation-solving task.

subcategory.description: Solve quadratic equations (including those that require rearrangement) algebraically by factorising, by completing the square, and by using the quadratic formula. Know the quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Find approximate solutions of quadratic equations using a graph.

assessment.dominant_operation: Solve a quadratic equation and retain both square-root solutions.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The target is an equation's solution set rather than evaluation of a numerical root.

subcategory.description: Solve quadratic equations (including those that require rearrangement) algebraically by factorising, by completing the square, and by using the quadratic formula. Know the quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Find approximate solutions of quadratic equations using a graph.

assessment.dominant_operation: Find both roots of a quadratic by factorisation.
assessment.why_not_alternative: This is a quadratic, not a general linear or simultaneous equation.

subcategory.description: Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions (y = mx + c) graphically and algebraically. Identify pairs of parallel lines and identify pairs of perpendicular lines, including the relationships between gradients. Find the equation of the line through two given points, or through one point with a given gradient.

assessment.dominant_operation: Relate the gradients of two linear equations using perpendicularity.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The gradient relation is the tested skill rather than coordinate geometry of a shape.

subcategory.description: Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions (y = mx + c) graphically and algebraically. Identify pairs of parallel lines and identify pairs of perpendicular lines, including the relationships between gradients. Find the equation of the line through two given points, or through one point with a given gradient.

assessment.dominant_operation: Construct the parallel line through a given coordinate.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Gradient and intercept constraints determine the line; generic equation solving is supporting work.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Substitute the known intersection into two linear equations to determine their parameters.
assessment.why_not_alternative: No gradient or intercept interpretation is needed; the two parameter equations are decisive.

subcategory.description: Simplify expressions involving sums, products and powers, including the laws of indices. Simplify rational expressions by cancelling, or factorising and cancelling. Use the four rules on algebraic rational expressions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Factor a polynomial and cancel against a symbolic radical denominator.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The task is symbolic rational-expression simplification, not numerical surd arithmetic.

subcategory.description: Rearrange formulae to change the subject.

assessment.dominant_operation: Rearrange the supplied curve equation to express y in terms of x.
assessment.why_not_alternative: No geometric property of the circle is required to isolate the subject.

subcategory.description: Know the formulae: a. circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd b. area of a circle = πr² c. volume of a right circular cylinder = πr²h Formulae relating to spheres, pyramids and cones will be given if needed. Use formulae to calculate: a. perimeters of 2-dimensional shapes, including circles b. areas of circles and composite shapes c. surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

assessment.dominant_operation: Calculate the shaded difference between an outer square and an inscribed circle.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Pythagoras helps obtain the radius, but composite area is the actual target.

subcategory.description: Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π. Simplify surd expressions involving squares, e.g. √12 = √(4×3) = √4√3 = 2√3, and rationalise denominators; for example, candidates could be asked to rationalise expressions such as: 3/√7, 5/(3+2√5), 7/(2−√3), 3/(√5−√2).

assessment.dominant_operation: Rationalise a numerical surd denominator.
assessment.why_not_alternative: There is no algebraic variable or rational function to simplify.

subcategory.description: Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π. Simplify surd expressions involving squares, e.g. √12 = √(4×3) = √4√3 = 2√3, and rationalise denominators; for example, candidates could be asked to rationalise expressions such as: 3/√7, 5/(3+2√5), 7/(2−√3), 3/(√5−√2).

assessment.dominant_operation: Simplify and combine exact numerical surd products and sums.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Ordinary arithmetic is subordinate to surd simplification.

subcategory.description: Know and use the trigonometric ratios: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse tan θ = opposite/adjacent Apply these to find angles and lengths in right-angled triangles and, where possible, general triangles in 2- and 3-dimensional figures. Know the exact values of sin θ and cos θ for θ = 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°. Know the exact values of tan θ for θ = 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°. Candidates are not expected to recall or use the sine or cosine rules.

assessment.dominant_operation: Split the isosceles 120-degree triangle into right triangles and use exact trigonometric ratios for its base.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The necessary angle-to-length relationship is trigonometric; a side-only Pythagorean calculation is insufficient.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The dominant task is joint probability for a die and a coin. The official specification contains no probability subcategory; M2.5 counting is only supporting work.
assessment.evidence:
A die is rolled and a coin is tossed. 
Find the probability that the die shows an odd number and the coin shows a head.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The dominant task is the probability of a restricted two-dice event. Counting outcomes alone does not cover the missing probability concept in the official taxonomy.
assessment.evidence:
Two six sided dice are rolled. 
What is the probability that both dice show odd numbers and their sum is less than 9?

subcategory.description: Use index laws in algebra for multiplication and division of integer, fractional, and negative powers.

assessment.dominant_operation: Apply index laws to a product and quotient with negative algebraic exponents.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The expression is governed by exponent laws rather than factoring a rational polynomial.

subcategory.description: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae. Understand and use the concepts and vocabulary: expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors.

assessment.dominant_operation: Substitute the three supplied numerical values into the expression.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Index arithmetic supports evaluating the specified substitution.

subcategory.description: Recall and use the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, perpendicular lines and opposite angles at a vertex. Understand and use the angle properties of parallel lines, intersecting lines, triangles and quadrilaterals. Calculate and use the sum of the interior angles, and the sum of the exterior angles, of polygons.

assessment.dominant_operation: Determine the relative positions of clock hands as angles about a point.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Time readings supply the context; the requested result is angular geometry.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Solve the two simultaneous linear equations for their common ordered pair.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The task asks for the common solution, not properties of the separate gradients.

subcategory.description: Factorise quadratic expressions of the form x²+bx+c, including the difference of two squares. Factorise quadratic expressions of the form ax²+bx+c, including the difference of two squares.

assessment.dominant_operation: Extract the common x and factor the remaining quadratic trinomial.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Common-factor extraction is preliminary to the dominant quadratic factorisation.

subcategory.description: Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of: a. linear functions b. quadratic functions c. simple cubic functions d. the reciprocal function: y = 1/x with x≠0 e. the exponential function: y = kˣ for positive values of k f. trigonometric functions (with arguments in degrees): y = sin x, y = cos x, y = tan x for angles of any size

assessment.dominant_operation: Interpret horizontal and vertical shifts of two quadratic function graphs.
assessment.why_not_alternative: These are algebraic graph forms rather than geometric congruence constructions.

subcategory.description: Recall and use the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, perpendicular lines and opposite angles at a vertex. Understand and use the angle properties of parallel lines, intersecting lines, triangles and quadrilaterals. Calculate and use the sum of the interior angles, and the sum of the exterior angles, of polygons.

assessment.dominant_operation: Use interior/exterior angle relations in a regular polygon.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Naming or defining the polygon is not the requested operation.

subcategory.description: Apply systematic listing strategies. (For instance, if there are m ways of doing one task and for each of these tasks there are n ways of doing another task, then the total number of ways the two tasks can be done in order is m× n ways.)

assessment.dominant_operation: Count overlapping finite sets systematically using inclusion and exclusion; no probability is requested
assessment.why_not_alternative: The dominant task is counting set membership; algebra only records the count relationships.

subcategory.description: Define percentage as ‘number of parts per hundred’. Interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal and interpret these multiplicatively. Express one quantity as a percentage of another. Compare two quantities using percentages. Work with percentages greater than 100%. Solve problems involving percentage change, including percentage increase/decrease, original value problems and simple interest calculations.

assessment.dominant_operation: Apply successive percentage decrease and increase to compare the result with the original.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Two stated percentage changes do not form a general growth/decay or iterative-process task.

subcategory.description: Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π. Simplify surd expressions involving squares, e.g. √12 = √(4×3) = √4√3 = 2√3, and rationalise denominators; for example, candidates could be asked to rationalise expressions such as: 3/√7, 5/(3+2√5), 7/(2−√3), 3/(√5−√2).

assessment.dominant_operation: Reduce square factors and collect numerical surd terms.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The surd structure, rather than routine integer arithmetic, is dominant.

subcategory.description: Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions (y = mx + c) graphically and algebraically. Identify pairs of parallel lines and identify pairs of perpendicular lines, including the relationships between gradients. Find the equation of the line through two given points, or through one point with a given gradient.

assessment.dominant_operation: Match a linear equation to its graph through its gradient and intercepts.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The specific linear gradient/intercept description is more precise than general graph recognition.

subcategory.description: Interpret, order and calculate with numbers written in standard index form (standard form); numbers are written in standard form as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.

assessment.dominant_operation: Compare decimal values expressed as multiples of powers of ten.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Scientific/index-form place value is the target rather than general index simplification.

assessment.reason: The decisive result is the polynomial remainder theorem p(x)=(x−1)q(x)+p(1), which is not stated in the official algebra subcategories. Substitution or identity notation alone does not capture it. The identified subject is not one of the four user-approved Other topic groups.

categorization_issues.reason: The decisive result is the polynomial remainder theorem p(x)=(x−1)q(x)+p(1), which is not stated in the official algebra subcategories. Substitution or identity notation alone does not capture it. The identified subject is not one of the four user-approved Other topic groups.

subcategory.description: Solve quadratic equations (including those that require rearrangement) algebraically by factorising, by completing the square, and by using the quadratic formula. Know the quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a). Find approximate solutions of quadratic equations using a graph.

assessment.dominant_operation: Construct a quadratic equation from the sum and product of its roots.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The roots-to-coefficients relation concerns the equation rather than graphical turning points.

subcategory.description: Know the formulae: a. circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd b. area of a circle = πr² c. volume of a right circular cylinder = πr²h Formulae relating to spheres, pyramids and cones will be given if needed. Use formulae to calculate: a. perimeters of 2-dimensional shapes, including circles b. areas of circles and composite shapes c. surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

assessment.dominant_operation: Equate cylinder surface-area and volume formulae to obtain the height relation.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The geometric formula model is necessary; rearranging the resulting equality is supporting algebra.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The task asks for probability of a colour composition in a random sample without replacement. The official taxonomy omits probability; systematic counting does not replace it.
assessment.evidence:
A bag contains 8 blue and 2 red balls. Three balls are chosen at the same time at random 
from the bag. What is the probability that exactly two of the balls are the same colour?

subcategory.description: Interpret, order and calculate with numbers written in standard index form (standard form); numbers are written in standard form as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.

assessment.dominant_operation: Calculate products and powers in scientific notation and express the answer in standard form.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Substitution is straightforward; standard-form arithmetic is the main burden.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Translate the total count and total coin value into simultaneous linear equations.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Arithmetic alone does not encode the two unknown coin counts.

subcategory.description: Know and use the formula for Pythagoras’ theorem: a² + b² = c². Use Pythagoras’ theorem in both 2 and 3 dimensions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Find a missing right-triangle side using the hypotenuse and another side.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Surd simplification supports Pythagoras rather than defining the target.

subcategory.description: Know and apply formulae to calculate: a. the area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia b. the volume of cuboids and other right prisms.

assessment.dominant_operation: Use the triangle area formula with the two displayed perpendicular side lengths.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Surd multiplication is supporting calculation after the geometric area relation.

subcategory.description: Calculate arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors of circles.

assessment.dominant_operation: Determine the sector angle and combine the complementary circular sector with the triangle.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The essential non-routine geometry is the fraction of the circle defined by the angle.

subcategory.description: Apply the four operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division) to integers, decimals, simple fractions (proper and improper) and mixed numbers – any of which could be positive and negative. Understand and use place value.

assessment.dominant_operation: Subtract the smallest two-digit odd integer from the largest three-digit even integer.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The task uses ordinary arithmetic/place value rather than a special cancellation or operation relationship.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The required binomial probability of exactly one illness in a sample of three is outside the official specification; fraction arithmetic is only supporting.
assessment.evidence:
In 2001 a quarter of the population of Wales reported having a limiting long-term illness or 
disability which restricted their daily activities. 
What is the probability that out of a random group of three people who live in Wales, exactly 
one of them will have reported such an illness or disability?

subcategory.description: Know the formulae: a. circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd b. area of a circle = πr² c. volume of a right circular cylinder = πr²h Formulae relating to spheres, pyramids and cones will be given if needed. Use formulae to calculate: a. perimeters of 2-dimensional shapes, including circles b. areas of circles and composite shapes c. surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

assessment.dominant_operation: Add a cylinder and hemisphere volume to form one composite solid.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Circular or composite area/perimeter/surface/volume is the principal objective.

subcategory.description: Use index laws in algebra for multiplication and division of integer, fractional, and negative powers.

assessment.dominant_operation: Express both sides as powers of three and equate algebraic exponents.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The index-law manipulation is algebraic with symbolic expressions or exponents.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Model consecutive integers by one linear unknown and impose the stated multiple relationship.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Solve/model linear or simultaneous constraints rather than a single quadratic equation.

subcategory.description: Know and use the formula for Pythagoras’ theorem: a² + b² = c². Use Pythagoras’ theorem in both 2 and 3 dimensions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Use the right triangle between tangent-circle centres to find the interstitial circle radius.
assessment.why_not_alternative: A right-triangle length relation is necessary; exact arithmetic with surds is supporting.

subcategory.description: Understand and use direct and inverse proportion, including algebraic representations. Recognise and interpret graphs that illustrate direct and inverse proportion. Set up, use and interpret equations to solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion (including questions involving integer and fractional powers). Understand that x is inversely proportional to y is equivalent to x is proportional to 1/y.

assessment.dominant_operation: Eliminate z between a direct square law and an inverse cube law.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The direct/inverse proportional relationship determines the model; arbitrary equation solving is supporting.

subcategory.description: Recall and use the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, perpendicular lines and opposite angles at a vertex. Understand and use the angle properties of parallel lines, intersecting lines, triangles and quadrilaterals. Calculate and use the sum of the interior angles, and the sum of the exterior angles, of polygons.

assessment.dominant_operation: Combine vertical angles, an exterior angle and the triangle angle sum.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Direct angle-sum/parallel/intersecting-line rules suffice without a congruence/similarity proof.

subcategory.description: Define percentage as ‘number of parts per hundred’. Interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal and interpret these multiplicatively. Express one quantity as a percentage of another. Compare two quantities using percentages. Work with percentages greater than 100%. Solve problems involving percentage change, including percentage increase/decrease, original value problems and simple interest calculations.

assessment.dominant_operation: Interpret an algebraic percentage statement and express the result as a percentage of the product.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Specified percentage changes/comparisons are tested rather than a recurring growth/decay process.

subcategory.description: Know and apply formulae to calculate: a. the area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia b. the volume of cuboids and other right prisms.

assessment.dominant_operation: Compare the feasible integer-sided rectangle areas and tile the rectangular sheet.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Use elementary triangle/quadrilateral/right-prism area or volume rather than circular/composite-solid formulae.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Use the positive-integer constraints to determine p and solve the remaining equation for q.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Solve/model linear or simultaneous constraints rather than a single quadratic equation.

subcategory.description: Understand and use direct and inverse proportion, including algebraic representations. Recognise and interpret graphs that illustrate direct and inverse proportion. Set up, use and interpret equations to solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion (including questions involving integer and fractional powers). Understand that x is inversely proportional to y is equivalent to x is proportional to 1/y.

assessment.dominant_operation: Scale the total book price directly with the number of identical books.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The direct/inverse proportional relationship determines the model; arbitrary equation solving is supporting.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The question requires joint probabilities with a biased die and normalisation of its outcome probabilities; no official probability subcategory exists.
assessment.evidence:
I have two six-sided dice, each with faces numbered from 1 to 6. One of the dice is fair, 
but the other is not – it will land on numbers 1 to 5 with equal probability, but lands on 6 with a 
different probability. 
When I roll the dice the probability that I get a total of 12 is $\frac{1}{18}$. What is the probability that I get a total of 2 when I roll the dice?

subcategory.description: Understand and use the basic congruence criteria for triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS).

assessment.dominant_operation: Test whether each equal-area and side/angle condition forces triangle congruence.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Determine whether the given conditions force triangle congruence, rather than compare scale factors.

subcategory.description: Set up and solve, both algebraically and graphically, simple equations including simultaneous equations involving two unknowns; this may include one linear and one quadratic equation. Solve two simultaneous equations in two variables (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically. Find approximate solutions using a graph. Translate simple situations or procedures into algebraic expressions or formulae; for example, derive an equation (or two simultaneous equations), solve the equation(s) and interpret the solution.

assessment.dominant_operation: Translate the vegetable count and total price into two linear equations.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Solve/model linear or simultaneous constraints rather than a single quadratic equation.

subcategory.description: Know the formulae: a. circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd b. area of a circle = πr² c. volume of a right circular cylinder = πr²h Formulae relating to spheres, pyramids and cones will be given if needed. Use formulae to calculate: a. perimeters of 2-dimensional shapes, including circles b. areas of circles and composite shapes c. surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

assessment.dominant_operation: Equate cone and sphere volumes and express the sphere radius.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Circular or composite area/perimeter/surface/volume is the principal objective.

subcategory.description: Know the formulae: a. circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd b. area of a circle = πr² c. volume of a right circular cylinder = πr²h Formulae relating to spheres, pyramids and cones will be given if needed. Use formulae to calculate: a. perimeters of 2-dimensional shapes, including circles b. areas of circles and composite shapes c. surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

assessment.dominant_operation: Calculate exposed surface area after subtracting joining faces in a composite of three cubes.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Circular or composite area/perimeter/surface/volume is the principal objective.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Statistics. Optimising a median under mean and range constraints requires statistical definitions and order statistics absent from the official subcategories.
assessment.evidence: A group of five numbers are such that: [LIST]What is the largest possible median of the five numbers?

subcategory.description: Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions. Understand and use the symbols: = , ≠ , < , > , ≤ , ≥ .

assessment.dominant_operation: Compare signs and magnitudes of products using the positions on the number line.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Ordering/sign comparison is decisive rather than evaluation of an arithmetic expression.

subcategory.description: Use index laws in algebra for multiplication and division of integer, fractional, and negative powers.

assessment.dominant_operation: Simplify a symbolic power quotient with negative and positive exponents.
assessment.why_not_alternative: The index-law manipulation is algebraic with symbolic expressions or exponents.

subcategory.description: Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions (y = mx + c) graphically and algebraically. Identify pairs of parallel lines and identify pairs of perpendicular lines, including the relationships between gradients. Find the equation of the line through two given points, or through one point with a given gradient.

assessment.dominant_operation: Find a line gradient from two points and use parallelism and the remaining point.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Gradient/intercept/line equation relationships are central rather than coordinate geometry of a shape.

subcategory.description: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors (divisors), multiples, common factors, common multiples, highest common factor, lowest common multiple, and prime factorisation (including use of product notation and the unique factorisation theorem).

assessment.dominant_operation: Determine parity possibilities using divisibility by two in a product and sum.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Divisibility, factors, multiples or parity supplies the necessary reasoning beyond routine arithmetic.

subcategory.description: Know and use the formula for Pythagoras’ theorem: a² + b² = c². Use Pythagoras’ theorem in both 2 and 3 dimensions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Set up the right-triangle side relation from the three algebraic lengths.
assessment.why_not_alternative: A right-triangle length relation is necessary; exact arithmetic with surds is supporting.

assessment.dominant_operation: Dominant topic: Probability. The dominant task is compound sampling probability without replacement across two baskets; the official taxonomy has no probability subcategory.
assessment.evidence:
Basket A contains 4 apples, 6 oranges, and 2 lemons. Basket B contains 5 apples, 4 oranges, 
and 6 lemons. You are to get two fruits from each basket. 
What is the probability of getting 2 oranges from Basket A and then 1 apple and 1 lemon from 
Basket B?

subcategory.description: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors (divisors), multiples, common factors, common multiples, highest common factor, lowest common multiple, and prime factorisation (including use of product notation and the unique factorisation theorem).

assessment.dominant_operation: Test integer factors of the given number.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Divisibility, factors, multiples or parity supplies the necessary reasoning beyond routine arithmetic.

subcategory.description: Recall and use the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, perpendicular lines and opposite angles at a vertex. Understand and use the angle properties of parallel lines, intersecting lines, triangles and quadrilaterals. Calculate and use the sum of the interior angles, and the sum of the exterior angles, of polygons.

assessment.dominant_operation: Calculate the angle between two clock hands at the stated time.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Direct angle-sum/parallel/intersecting-line rules suffice without a congruence/similarity proof.

subcategory.description: Know and use the formula for Pythagoras’ theorem: a² + b² = c². Use Pythagoras’ theorem in both 2 and 3 dimensions.

assessment.dominant_operation: Use the base diagonal and a sloping edge to obtain a pyramid's perpendicular height.
assessment.why_not_alternative: A right-triangle length relation is necessary; exact arithmetic with surds is supporting.

subcategory.description: Recognise and use relationships between operations, including inverse operations. Use cancellation to simplify calculations and expressions. Understand and use the convention for priority of operations, including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals.

assessment.dominant_operation: Exploit distributive/product relationships between nearby integers in the large calculation.
assessment.why_not_alternative: Operation structure, cancellation or distributive rearrangement is the decisive efficient calculation.
